aggregation: MicroSeries.sum and MicroSeries.groupby(source household).sum on analysis flags in each part's frozen simulation, with map_to='person' for residents; stored weight columns are not read.

groups.added_by_job: Households in the combined set but not its raise-only counterpart (combined vs raise_union, combined_1000 vs raise_1000).
groups.additional_below_half: Households below 50% on any test in the set, excluding every household below 0% on any test in the set; residents counted once; measured directly as its own household set.
groups.below_half_total: Households below 50% on any test in the set (strict plus additional).
groups.strict_loss: Households below 0% retention on any test in the set; residents counted once.

measures.with_health: Government-valued health coverage, ACA PTC counted once (d_net_single_ptc).
measures.without_health: Every part of net income except health benefits and costs (d_net_without_health).

question: People in households that trip the raise test or the job test under 2017 federal rules, each person counted once.
retention: Change in household resources divided by the gross pay change; a household trips a test at t when any tested adult's household keeps strictly less than t.

scope: Finite grid of raises and one job offer per eligible adult; no claim about other raise sizes, untested adults, additional childcare costs or new employer coverage.
status_note: All 51 jurisdictions, every invariant passed and the raise union reproduced exactly; final numbers pending independent review.

tests.job: A working-age adult (18-64) with no wages or self-employment income, excluding full-time students and people reporting disability, takes a full-time job (40 hours x 52 weeks) at the state's 2017 minimum wage, one adult at a time.
tests.raise: A current worker among the household's two highest-earning adults (by market income) gets a $1,000, $2,000 or $5,000 raise, one adult at a time.

uncertainty.method: percentile; multinomial resample of all source households jointly, one draw for every count (scripts/driver_intervals.resample, batched)
